title: Stream ledger exports instead of building them in memory
intent: The export used to collect every row before writing the file. It now writes rows as the cursor yields them, so memory stays flat however large the ledger is.

sections.title: Why memory grew with the ledger
sections.overview: The export read the whole ledger into one array before it wrote a byte. Memory grew with the row count, and the March ledger did not fit on the small worker.

diffs.summary: The docs now say how the export reads and writes.

sections.title: The streaming writer
sections.overview: The writer takes rows from the database cursor and flushes every 500 rows. A failed write closes the cursor and removes the partial file, so a half export is never left behind.

diffs.summary: Replaces the in-memory array with a cursor loop and a flush every 500 rows.
Covers the flush size, a failed write and memory on a large ledger.

sections.title: A failed write leaves no partial file
sections.overview: Removing the partial file must not fail when the write failed before the file existed.

diffs.summary: A file that is already gone is fine.
The case where nothing was written.

sections.title: Memory on the March ledger
sections.overview: The benchmark now runs the streaming export. Peak memory went from 1.9 GB to 140 MB.

diffs.summary: Labels the run and records the numbers.
